title: Pork chops with fennel and pea rice

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a plain whole food or cupboard staple, and chicken stock counts as good stock.

supermarket.reason: Pork chops, fennel, basmati, frozen peas and the rest are everyday Tesco lines at ordinary prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only one wide lidded pan, and browning and simmering are well within a beginner's reach.

works.reason: 300g rice with 750ml stock, simmered covered for about 20 minutes with the chops on top, gives a soft one-pot rice and cooked-through chops for four, though it may be on the moist side.

honest_times.reason: Slicing two fennel bulbs and garlic, browning the chops, softening and finishing fit in 20 active minutes, and the 10 plus 8 to 10 minute simmers match the 20 cook minutes.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used, the names match their ids (basmati under long-grain-rice is allowed), and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: Fennel, doubled up with fennel seeds and paired with peas and lemon, is the point of a light midsummer dinner.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear British English with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Pork, rice, fennel and peas make a balanced, filling family dinner.
